sections.title: Physiotherapy
sections.intro: Physiotherapy focuses on movement, physical function and participation. Therapy may address mobility, balance, coordination, posture, strength, gross motor development and confidence in physical activities.

sections.title: Support built around everyday participation.
sections.intro: Therapy goals are individual. These examples show common areas that may be explored when they are relevant to the person and their priorities.

items.title: Mobility
items.description: Walking, transfers and functional movement across everyday environments.

items.title: Balance & coordination
items.description: Developing body control, stability and coordinated movement.

items.title: Strength & endurance
items.description: Building physical capacity for daily activities, recreation and participation.

items.title: Gross motor skills
items.description: Running, jumping, stairs, playground skills and age-appropriate movement patterns.

items.title: Postural control
items.description: Support for posture, core stability and efficient movement.

items.title: Physical participation
items.description: Helping people take part more confidently in home, school and community activities.

panels.title: Goals first, service second.
paragraphs: Physiotherapy can be adapted to different ages, abilities and functional goals, subject to clinician availability and individual assessment.
We start by understanding what is working well, what feels difficult and what meaningful change would look like in daily life. From there, the clinician can recommend a suitable next step.

items.title: Start with your priorities
items.description: Tell us what matters, what is currently difficult and what you hope to change.

items.title: Understand strengths & needs
items.description: Your clinician gathers relevant information and completes assessment where appropriate.

items.title: Build practical strategies
items.description: Sessions focus on meaningful goals and strategies that make sense in real routines.

items.title: Review & adapt
items.description: Progress is reviewed together and the plan is adjusted as needs and goals change.

sections.title: Before you get started.
sections.intro: These answers are general. We can discuss individual circumstances when you contact the team.

items.question: Does physiotherapy only happen in the clinic?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Depending on the service plan, useful strategies can be designed around everyday environments and routines.

items.question: Will I receive exercises to practise at home?
items.answer: Where appropriate, your physiotherapist may recommend simple activities or exercises to reinforce therapy goals between sessions.

items.question: Can physiotherapy work alongside OT or Exercise Physiology?
items.answer: Yes. When useful, disciplines can coordinate goals so support remains clear and complementary.
